questions.prompt: What does `*args` capture in a Python function?
options: Extra positional arguments as a tuple
Extra keyword arguments as a dict
questions.answer: Extra positional arguments as a tuple
questions.explanation: `*args` gathers extra positional arguments into a tuple. It is useful for wrappers and flexible APIs.

concept_panel.title: *args
concept_panel.explanation: `*args` gathers extra positional arguments into a tuple. It is useful for wrappers and flexible APIs.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand Python call binding.

options: Extra keyword arguments as a dictionary
questions.answer: Extra keyword arguments as a dictionary
questions.explanation: `**kwargs` gathers extra keyword arguments into a dictionary. It is common in decorators and API adapters.

concept_panel.title: **kwargs
concept_panel.explanation: `**kwargs` gathers extra keyword arguments into a dictionary. It is common in decorators and API adapters.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand flexible function APIs.

options: To prevent callers from depending on parameter names
questions.answer: To prevent callers from depending on parameter names
questions.explanation: Positional-only parameters let API authors change internal parameter names without breaking callers.

concept_panel.title: Positional-only Args
concept_panel.explanation: Positional-only parameters let API authors change internal parameter names without breaking callers.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand public API compatibility.

options: To force clarity at call sites
questions.answer: To force clarity at call sites
questions.explanation: Keyword-only arguments are useful for flags and options where positional calls would be ambiguous.

concept_panel.title: Keyword-only Args
concept_panel.explanation: Keyword-only arguments are useful for flags and options where positional calls would be ambiguous.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can design readable function interfaces.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with `def add_item(item, bucket=[]): bucket.append(item)`?
options: The same list is reused across calls
The list is copied every call
Default arguments are evaluated at return time
questions.answer: The same list is reused across calls
questions.explanation: Default argument values are evaluated once when the function is defined. Mutable defaults can accidentally share state.

concept_panel.title: Default Argument Pitfall
concept_panel.explanation: Default argument values are evaluated once when the function is defined. Mutable defaults can accidentally share state.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use `bucket=None` and create a new list inside.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know one of Python's most common production bugs.

options: A replacement for every named function
questions.explanation: Lambdas are anonymous single-expression functions. They are useful when concise and harmful when they reduce readability.

concept_panel.title: Lambda Functions
concept_panel.explanation: Lambdas are anonymous single-expression functions. They are useful when concise and harmful when they reduce readability.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you balance Pythonic syntax with maintainability.

questions.prompt: What does `[x * x for x in nums if x > 0]` create?
questions.explanation: List comprehensions build a list immediately. They are concise but still allocate the full result.

concept_panel.title: List Comprehension
concept_panel.explanation: List comprehensions build a list immediately. They are concise but still allocate the full result.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know comprehension behavior and memory cost.

questions.prompt: Which expression builds a lookup by user id?
questions.explanation: Dict comprehensions create key-value mappings. They are useful for fast lookup by ID.

concept_panel.title: Dict Comprehension
concept_panel.explanation: Dict comprehensions create key-value mappings. They are useful for fast lookup by ID.
concept_panel.practical_example: users_by_id = {u.id: u for u in users}
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can transform data into useful access structures.

questions.explanation: Set comprehensions produce unique values. They are useful for deduplication.

concept_panel.title: Set Comprehension
concept_panel.explanation: Set comprehensions produce unique values. They are useful for deduplication.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know collection-specific comprehensions.

questions.prompt: Why use `(row.id for row in rows)`?
questions.explanation: Generator expressions produce one value at a time and can reduce memory pressure.

concept_panel.title: Generator Expressions
concept_panel.explanation: Generator expressions produce one value at a time and can reduce memory pressure.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand lazy iteration.

questions.prompt: Which exception handler is best practice?
options: Catch the specific exception you can handle
Catch all exceptions and ignore them
questions.answer: Catch the specific exception you can handle
questions.explanation: Specific exception handling keeps unexpected bugs visible while handling known failures cleanly.

concept_panel.title: Exceptions
concept_panel.explanation: Specific exception handling keeps unexpected bugs visible while handling known failures cleanly.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you handle errors intentionally.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a virtual environment?
questions.explanation: Virtual environments keep dependencies per project. Packages and modules organize code, and `__init__.py` initializes package namespaces.

concept_panel.title: Packages and Virtual Environments
concept_panel.explanation: Virtual environments keep dependencies per project. Packages and modules organize code, and `__init__.py` initializes package namespaces.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use `.venv` so FastAPI dependencies do not conflict with another project.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can structure and run Python projects reliably.
